### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c347d22d2bcce32b414e693f2ec5ca5f564db53a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b4d952cb8f42b03d73afbfc1b9c53e641b67e7be` — the merge of head `214ca68802758ad6eca5333b2135bec5753ee666` into base `c347d22d2bcce32b414e693f2ec5ca5f564db53a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b4d952cb8f42b03d73afbfc1b9c53e641b67e7be && git checkout b4d952cb8f42b03d73afbfc1b9c53e641b67e7be
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c347d22d2bcce32b414e693f2ec5ca5f564db53a 214ca68802758ad6eca5333b2135bec5753ee666 && git checkout -B drift-repro c347d22d2bcce32b414e693f2ec5ca5f564db53a && git merge --no-ff 214ca68802758ad6eca5333b2135bec5753ee666

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c347d22d2bcce32b414e693f2ec5ca5f564db53a
```

</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8d01f7cfd2c5a5b27c702234b2a7c63400818e76`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-cap.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invite-role-not-found-code.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/accept-invitation-adopt-membership.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/invitation-blank-role-refusal.dogfood.test.ts + better-auth 1.7.12 `dist/plugins/organization/routes/crud-invites.mjs` and `crud-members.mjs` (the vendor doors the hunks cite; read from the registry tarball, nothing run), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/adopt-membership.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-invitation.object.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/organization.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts

Reviewed at 2026-11-02T11:29Z. Inputs: card #29158 (body and every comment), PR #29296 (body, file list, net diff against `main`), the check-runs on the head. Not the dispatch order.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member` narrows** — a role value whose whole string is empty or whitespace, an empty role array, or a role list with one empty entry, is refused 400 `ROLE_NOT_FOUND` before `adapter.createInvitation`; no `sys_invitation` row. **Right.** The vendor's body schema (`z.union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])`) admits `""`, and its role check (`parseRoles` → `split(',').map(trim).filter(Boolean)`) drops exactly the entries `hasBlankInvitationRoleEntry` refuses, so on `main` those shapes named no unknown role and were stored verbatim as `role: ''` / `'member,'`. The new guard's predicate is the vendor's drop predicate inverted (same `trim`), so the two agree on every string; a non-string role never reaches the hook (the zod body schema refuses it first), and `hasBlankInvitationRoleEntry` correctly answers `false` for it rather than claiming a verdict.
- **No widening anywhere.** Every named role is judged as before: the vocabulary (ADR-0108), the cap's three refusals, the placement gate. The control cases (`admin` by the owner, `member` on both postures) pin it.
- **Error-code surface: no new code.** `ROLE_NOT_FOUND` is already in the ledger (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, registered for this door by #24750) and is the code the spec's invitation `role` docstring promises "at the door, before any invitation row exists". The message keeps the vendor's `ROLE_NOT_FOUND: ` prefix. **Right.** The thrown `APIError` carries `code`, so the after-hook `codeInviteRoleNotFound` (which only stamps an uncoded vendor refusal) leaves it untouched — no double handling.
- **Hook order** — cloud-managed → blank role → role cap → placement gate. **Right.** A delegated admin's blank role answers `ROLE_NOT_FOUND`, not the cap's 403 (pinned); the cap's own "not a reachable shape" comment, which was false, is corrected to point at the guard that now runs first.
- **Resend** — the vendor's `resend: true` branch for an already-pending invitee updates `expiresAt` and returns before `beforeCreateInvitation`, writing no role; a resend with no pending row (or an expired one, #28540) creates a new invitation and meets the guard. **Right**, as the PR states.
- **Other doors that write a membership or invitation role, read for a blank that still gets through:** `update-member-role` — the vendor refuses an empty `roleToSet` with 400 before any write (`crud-members.mjs`); `add-member` — a pathless endpoint, server-only, not reachable over HTTP; `admin-import-users` — writes the admin plugin's user role via `createUser` and drops an empty one (a zero-length `data.role` becomes `undefined`), never a `sys_invitation` row; the data API serves `sys_invitation` get/list only. No direct `createInvitation` caller in the tree outside the vendor route. **None found open.**
- **Public exports** — `hasBlankInvitationRoleEntry`, `blankInvitationRoleRefusal`, `InviteRoleRefusal` are new exports of an internal module; `@objectstack/plugin-auth`'s index does not re-export them (no public API surface moves). No `packages/spec/**` edit; no schema key moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is **right**: the role rides an HTTP body, not anything a metadata author writes.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29158-invite-blank-role-refused.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, BREAKING banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), a remedy line. Per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3 a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition — **the level matches what the diff publishes.** Nothing authorable is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO map or tombstone is owed. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- `Clause-②:` line — `no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, the measured arm (base 200 and a row; head 400 and no row) — **right**.
- **should-fix (prose, not a FAIL):** the changeset's Before paragraph and its `Clause-②:` sentence say a role list with an empty entry such as `"member,"` "answered 200 and stored the invitation". On the composed stack that shape was already refused on base — by the `sys_invitation.role` select validator (`record-validator.ts`: a blank is "missing" and the field is `required: false`, so `''` passes; `'member,'` is not an option, so `invalid_option` → 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`). Only the whole-value blanks (`""`, whitespace) were accepted there; the list-entry shapes were stored only on a composition without the ObjectQL validator. A client branching on `error.code` sees `VALIDATION_FAILED` become `ROLE_NOT_FOUND` for that shape, which the "Who sees it" paragraph should name in one line. The level does not move.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 — `"member,"` / `",admin"` already refused 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` on base, now 400 `ROLE_NOT_FOUND`: keep the code change?** Keep it (the dev's first option), and it is acceptable under the declared level. The status and the zero-row outcome are unchanged; what moves is the code, from a write-time validator's generic refusal to the door's own code — the one the spec's `role` docstring already promises for a role that names no role, before any row. One code for "the role names nothing" on this door is the ADR-0112 shape; a client that branched on `VALIDATION_FAILED` for a comma-trailing role was branching on an accident of the write path, not on a published promise. A non-protocol code move on an already-refused input is covered by `patch` + BREAKING banner; it owes the one line in the changeset named in ②. The alternative (leave list entries to the validator) would make the door's answer depend on which composition sits behind it, which is the worse contract.
- **Open question 2 — default a blank role to `member` instead?** No: refuse, as shipped. The card's security floor, the seat's order and the spec's "refused at the door" docstring all say refuse; `isPlainMemberInvitation` and the cap stay untouched; defaulting would be a product choice with no caller shown to rely on it.
- **Deviation: ablation redone with a string marker after a comment marker was stripped by the bundler** — right call; the discarded reading was discarded, the redone one went red on every blank case and restored to a HEAD-equal blob.
- **Deviation: `--workspace-concurrency` placement** — tooling, no bearing on the diff.
- **Deviation: no MCP write, no assignee** — correct under the standard order.
- **Out-of-scope finding: invitations already stored with `role: ''`** are not rewritten and still accept into a role-less membership under a wall. Answered: no door writes a new one now, acceptance confers less (never more) privilege, and an operator can cancel a pending blank row from the Invitations list; nothing is owed by this PR. Escalation left to the seat's discretion (a backfill or cancel-on-boot card); not a condition of this verdict.
- **Out-of-scope finding: other `sys_invitation.role` writers** — confirmed in ① from the cited code.
- **Seat order's stop lines** (no `packages/spec/**`, no new code, no better-auth or overrides change, no defaulting): all held in the committed tree.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts`** — the guard sits where the vendor hands over `invitation.role` as the joined string (`roles = parseRoles(ctx.body.role)`) and before `adapter.createInvitation`, so an array body is already flattened and no row exists when it throws. The `cancelPendingInvitationsOnReInvite` path and the expired-row re-issue both run through the hook; the pending-row resend returns earlier and writes no role. Against the card's scenario (owner or delegated admin, single and walled `group`, `""`), the request is refused in the hook on every path that would write a role. Tried: role given as a number or object (zod body schema refuses the shape first, the guard correctly abstains), `[" "]` (joined to `" "`, refused), `"member,,admin"` (refused — the same entry the vendor would drop), a Unicode space `trim()` removes (refused, the vendor would have dropped it), a zero-width space (`trim()` keeps it on both sides, so the vendor refuses it as an unknown role). **Holds. No finding.**
- **`invite-role-not-found-code.ts`** — `hasBlankInvitationRoleEntry` flattens an array the way the vendor's `parseRoles` does and asks the vendor's own drop predicate; `blankInvitationRoleRefusal` answers the ledger code with the vendor's prefix so the body shape is byte-compatible with the unknown-role refusal the same module codes. The two functions are pure and asked once per request. **Holds. No finding.**
- **`invitation-role-cap.ts`** — comment only; the new sentence is true against the vendor source (body schema admits `""`, the check drops empties) and names the guard that runs first. `requested.length === 0 → null` is now genuinely unreachable from the door for a blank role (refused upstream) and remains the right fail-open-to-nothing answer for a direct caller. **Holds. No finding.**
- **`accept-invitation-adopt-membership.test.ts`** — the new block runs the real `AuthManager` and vendor route (nothing on the path stubbed), covers all six blank shapes plus the delegate ordering case plus a named-role control, and asserts code, message prefix and zero rows. The dev reports it red on base (7 failed) and under ablation, which the mechanism predicts. **Holds. No finding.**
- **`invitation-blank-role-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`** — the composed CRM stack on both postures with the ObjectQL validator in the loop, a posture guard, three blank shapes refused with no row, a `member` control with exactly one pending row, env restored after. This is the file that pins the `"member,"` code move judged in ③. **Holds. No finding.**

No must-fix. One should-fix (② changeset prose).

Check-runs on the head at post time: 49 total, all complete — 36 success, 13 skipped (UI, docs, opt-in and sharded-matrix placeholders), 0 failure, 0 in progress. Among the green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Lint · ESLint, Type Check · workspace, Test Core 1–8/8, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate. These conclusions are the gate verdicts this record relies on; nothing was run locally.
